title: st.code modifies text when copied.
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

The st.code function modifies the text that is placed in it.  It appears to only be trailing text.  The issue is that I have a use case that has code/text that is CRC verified so it is not OK to delete things, even if they are white space.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

foo = "hello world   "  # <--- trailing space in string
st.code(foo)
```


### Steps To Reproduce

Run the above code.
Press the copy button in the top right of the code widget.

### Expected Behavior

The clipboard should have the text
`hello world    `

### Current Behavior

The clipboard has the text
`hello world`

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info


Version 1.33
Python 3.10
OS= Windows
Browser Chrome

### Additional Information

I would like an extra keyword parameter called something like "frozen," which could be set to true and make the passed-in immutable. It should default False to keep the current behavior.
